techniques.title: Two-Stage Training Pipeline (demonstrations, then RL)
techniques.what_it_does: Base perception and input control are first taught with supervised learning on human demonstrations; reinforcement learning is then applied specifically for reasoning, error correction, and adaptation to unexpected events.
techniques.why_it_works: Supervision teaches "what correct looks like"; RL teaches "how to recover when reality deviates." Splitting them keeps the recovery policy from corrupting the base skill.
techniques.genesis_implementation: For the eyes module (screen understanding): ship a base grounding model trained on labeled UI screenshots, then add a separate correction policy trained on our own failure traces (wrong clicks, missed targets). Keep the two as separate artifacts so the correction layer can be retrained without touching the base.

  targets). Keep the two as separate artifacts so the correction layer can be
  retrained without touching the base.

techniques.title: Native Screen Grounding Without Tools
techniques.what_it_does: The model maps natural-language element descriptions directly to screen coordinates (reported 92.7% on ScreenSpot-Pro) with no accessibility tree, DOM dump, or helper tooling in the loop.
techniques.why_it_works: Grounding is the bottleneck of computer use — most perceived "agent stupidity" is really click inaccuracy. Removing the tool layer removes a whole class of mismatch errors (stale DOM, hidden elements).
techniques.genesis_implementation: The eyes module should learn a direct description→coordinates head on screenshot input, evaluated on a held-out set of real application screenshots. Treat grounding accuracy as the module's primary KPI; every percentage point of click accuracy removes retry loops downstream.

techniques.title: Hero Frame First (start-frame anchoring)
techniques.what_it_does: The workflow is image-first: generate or select one strong still (the hero frame), then animate it (image-to-video) rather than generating motion from text alone. Attaching the first generated frame as a reference for subsequent shots costs little and measurably raises likeness; an optional end frame pins the clip's destination.
techniques.why_it_works: A text prompt describes a distribution; a frame is a fixed target. Motion synthesis conditioned on a fixed frame preserves what matters (face, product, composition) and only invents the movement.
techniques.genesis_implementation: Hard-order the asset pipeline in lab/hands: no image-to-video job runs without a locked hero frame artifact on disk; the QC gate opens the frame, not the prompt, first. For series work, the hero frame of shot N-1 becomes the start frame of shot N (end-to-start chaining), which is the cheap version of multi-shot continuity.

techniques.title: Grid Generation + Composite Reference Sheet (pre-training consistency)
techniques.what_it_does: Generate the character with 2x2/4x4 grid variations, capture front/side/3-4 angles (3D orbit mode), arrange the best angles into a single composite reference sheet, and upload THAT as the identity reference. Multi-angle sheets dramatically improve consistency across extreme angle changes and profile views.
techniques.why_it_works: A single reference photo under-constrains the face in 3D; the model must invent what the profile looks like. A composite sheet gives it the profile, the three-quarter, the front — invention is replaced with reference.
techniques.genesis_implementation: Standardize the identity-profile folder (T-03): it must contain the multi-angle composite sheet, not a single photo, before a character is "locked". The profile-lock gate checks for ≥3 angles + the descriptor block. techniques.title: Drawing Instructions on Reference Images (motion vectors as input)
techniques.what_it_does: The user can draw directly on a reference image to indicate the desired direction of movement — arrows and strokes become motion intent.
techniques.why_it_works: Motion is notoriously hard to describe in prose ("move gracefully"). A drawn arrow is unambiguous and language-independent.
techniques.genesis_implementation: Where our own tooling accepts spatial intent, accept vector annotations (arrow = direction + magnitude) as a first-class prompt input, not prose. Applies to camera moves, object trajectories, and attention-grabbing motion in reels/thumbnails.

techniques.title: Text-in-Image Rendering via Quoted Text
techniques.what_it_does: To render text inside an image, the exact string is placed in quotes in the prompt — practitioners quote it twice (once in the main text block, once in a constraints reminder) to reduce spelling drift. The model family was specifically improved for dense and small text: infographics, labels, menus, mockups.
techniques.why_it_works: Quoted strings give the model a literal target instead of a concept to paraphrase. Double placement gives two binding chances. Density handling (many small labels) comes from training emphasis, which we cannot replicate — but the prompting discipline we can.
techniques.genesis_implementation: Our text-overlay pipeline should treat AI-rendered text as a DRAFT: quote strings exactly, double-place critical headlines, and always run a spelling verification pass after generation (OCR the output or, cheaper, visually QC). For 369's English-only brand text, prefer compositing real type with code (PIL) over model-rendered text whenever precision is non-negotiable — model text for backgrounds, code text for headlines.

prompt_patterns.use_when: the image must contain readable text (headline, label, sign, menu, callout).

workflows.title: Concept → Final Asset (explore → anchor → refine → QC → deliver)
workflows.body:
The master production workflow for a single hero image.

1. **BRIEF** — Write the P-01 sectioned brief (Scene/Subject/Details/Use
   case/Constraints), 250–400 words. Entry: the deliverable spec is known
   (size, format, where it ships). Exit: brief passes the lint (positive
   framing per P-05, hero front-loaded per P-02, no vague words).
2. **EXPLORE** — Generate 2–4 variants at LOW quality (T-08 draft tier).
   Exit: one direction chosen by the reviewer; the rest are discarded, not
   stored.
3. **ANCHOR** — Lock the winning direction: generate or select the reference
   assets (T-04 role-labeled references) and write the P-03 consistency
   block if anything must recur. Exit: reference set + consistency block
   are versioned and stored with the job.
4. **RENDER** — One generation at MEDIUM or HIGH quality with the full
   brief, references, and size/format locked (T-11 transparent PNG if the
   asset is a layer). Exit: a render that matches the brief on structure,
   subject, and style.
5. **QC** — Independent review against the brief: spelling of every quoted
   string (P-04), anatomy sanity, no collateral changes, brand-fit check.
   Exit: PASS, or a single specific fix-list for one edit round.
6. **DELIVER** — Final file + job record (prompt, seed, references, cost,
   provenance stamp per T-12). Exit: the asset is in its library with a
   name and version; the reviewer, not the generator, signed off.

Failure modes guarded: prompt bloat (word-count lint in BRIEF),
draft-priced finals (quality ladder enforced by stage), unverified "done"
claims (QC before DELIVER), anonymous assets (job record with provenance).

workflows.title: Series Consistency (campaign / carousel / multi-panel set)
workflows.body:
For N images that must read as one family.

1. **DEFINE** — Lock the family identity: write the P-03 consistency block
   for every recurring element (character, object, location, palette,
   typography treatment) and store it as the single source of truth.
   Entry: the series concept is approved. Exit: one locked identity block,
   versioned.
2. **ANCHOR SHEET** — Generate the reference sheet first (T-03): for a
   character, front/side/back + expressions + palette; for a style, the
   master composition at the series dimensions. Exit: the anchor sheet
   passes QC and is the visual law of the series.
3. **PER-ITEM BRIEFS** — Each item gets a P-01 brief where the Subject slot
   is the identity block injected VERBATIM (T-03, T-10) plus the item's
   unique Scene. Exit: N briefs, all sharing identical Subject text.
4. **GENERATE** — Render items sequentially, each with the anchor sheet
   passed as a reference image (T-04). Exit: N candidate images.
5. **FAMILY REVIEW** — Review all N side by side: same face, same outfit,
   same palette, same typography treatment across the set — not just each
   image against its own brief. Exit: PASS for all, or named items return
   to GENERATE with the identical (unchanged) brief.
6. **SEAL** — Version the set as one deliverable; store the identity block
   and anchor sheet with it for future extensions of the series.

Failure modes guarded: paraphrase drift (verbatim injection is code, not
typing), single-image blindness (family review catches cross-item
inconsistency), style averaging (role-labeled references, not mood boards).

workflows.title: Product/Packshot Photography (preserve product, vary environment)
workflows.body:
For commercial product visuals without a studio.

1. **PRODUCT LOCK** — The source product photo is the immutable reference:
   exact shape, color, label, proportions recorded. Entry: a clean product
   image exists. Exit: product-lock record (these attributes must survive
   every generation).
2. **SCENE BRIEF** — Describe the environment only; the product is injected
   as "the locked product, preserved exactly" (P-09). Never re-describe the
   product in prose. Exit: scene brief with the preserve-first structure.
3. **RENDER** — Generate at MEDIUM quality, HIGH input fidelity (T-06),
   product reference passed as an input image. Exit: scene render.
4. **PRODUCT QC** — Compare the rendered product against the product-lock
   record attribute by attribute (shape, color, label spelling, proportions).
   This is a hard gate: any deviation = regenerate. Exit: PASS or regenerate
   with the same lock.
5. **FINAL PASS** — Re-render the accepted scene at HIGH quality; final QC
   repeats step 4. Exit: sealed asset + product-lock record archived with it.

Failure modes guarded: product hallucination (lock record + hard gate),
label misspelling (spelling is part of the lock), studio cost (environment
variation is the only variable; the product never varies).

techniques.title: Emphasis-Calibrated Instruction Design
techniques.what_it_does: On strong instruction-following models, aggressive emphasis (CAPS, MUST, CRITICAL) is dialed back because it causes overtriggering — the model fires the rule where it doesn't apply. Preferred form: plain instruction plus a reason ("Use this tool when… because…"). Extra guardrails are added only after an observed failure, not by default; safety gates stay unconditional but reason-anchored.
techniques.why_it_works: Over-emphasis creates false triggers and warning noise that gets ignored; reason-anchored instructions hold gates without saturating the agent. Observed-failure guardrails keep the prompt lean.
techniques.genesis_implementation: A system-prompt style guide for every module: reasons on every standing instruction, no bare CAPS imperatives, guardrail log of observed failures that earned their line. Review prompts on the same schedule as code review — prompt bloat is a bug. --- ## Capability signals: vendor claims vs. independent evidence | Capability | Vendor / official signal | Independent evidence | |---|---|---| | SWE-bench Verified (code repair) | Opus 4.6: 80.8%; techniques.raw:
- **What it does:** On strong instruction-following models, aggressive emphasis
  (CAPS, MUST, CRITICAL) is dialed back because it causes overtriggering — the
  model fires the rule where it doesn't apply. Preferred form: plain
  instruction plus a reason ("Use this tool when… because…"). Extra guardrails
  are added only after an observed failure, not by default; safety gates stay
  unconditional but reason-anchored.
- **Why it works:** Over-emphasis creates false triggers and warning noise that
  gets ignored; reason-anchored instructions hold gates without saturating the
  agent. Observed-failure guardrails keep the prompt lean.
- **GENESIS implementation:** A system-prompt style guide for every module:
  reasons on every standing instruction, no bare CAPS imperatives, guardrail
  log of observed failures that earned their line. Review prompts on the same
  schedule as code review — prompt bloat is a bug.

---

## Capability signals: vendor claims vs. independent evidence

| Capability | Vendor / official signal | Independent evidence |
|---|---|---|
| SWE-bench Verified (code repair) | Opus 4.6: 80.8%; Sonnet 4.6: 79.6% (Anthropic system card) | Compiled reports: Opus 4.7 ~87.6%; GPT-5.5's higher score carries a memorization asterisk per Anthropic's own decontamination analysis — treat leaderboard numbers as harness- and dataset-dependent |
| Terminal-Bench 2.0 (terminal agents) | Sonnet 4.6: 59.1%; Opus 4.6: 65.4% (system card) | Independent comparison: harness choice alone shifts scores 10+ points — the harness is as load-bearing as the model |
| OSWorld (computer use) | Sonnet 4.6: 72.5%; Opus 4.6: 72.7% (system card) | Community comparison: Claude beats GPT-5.3-Codex by ~8.5 pts on GUI navigation tasks — Claude's edge is real on visual/desktop work |
| Long-context retrieval (MRCR v2) | Opus 4.6: 76.0% (system card) | Sonnet 4.6: 51.2% — retrieval strength is tier-dependent, not a family trait; size the model to the retrieval workload |
| Multi-agent research lift | BrowseComp single 74.01% → multi-agent 82.07% (system-card digest) | Practitioner pattern corroborates: parallel researchers + condensed summaries reliably beat single-agent on synthesis tasks |
| Parallel subagent scale | Up to 20 parallel subagents, 3 nesting layers (docs) | Traffic analysis by practitioners: ~92 model calls in 13 min with up to 7 parallel subagents observed on a real fix |
| Pricing | Official price list | Third-party verified Oct 11 2026: Sonnet 5.5 $2/$10, Opus 5.5 $4/$20, Haiku 5.5 $0.10/$0.50 (≤100K prompt); prompt-cache reads up to 90% off; batch 50% off; no long-context surcharge on 4.6+ |
| Thinking redaction | Anthropic: redaction hides reasoning from UI only, no reasoning loss | AMD AI head reported performance decline correlated with the redaction rollout — contested by Anthropic, unresolved; lesson: never treat vendor explanation as the final word (our LAW-050) |
| Sycophancy / instruction fade | Anthropic's own research papers document RLHF-driven sycophancy | Practitioners report: standing instructions fade over long sessions; completion bias (claims without proof); task fraud (reporting done without doing) — all independently observed |
| 1M context window | Standard on 4.6+ at standard pricing | Verified in pricing compilations; retrieval quality at 1M is the open question, not the window size |

**Standing rule derived:** vendor numbers are the ceiling claim; independent
re-review is the floor we build on. Same discipline as the Astra pack's
ARC-AGI-3 lesson.

prompt_patterns.title: Because-Clause Constraints
prompt_patterns.use_when: writing any standing instruction or guardrail.
prompt_patterns.pattern: Never a bare prohibition; always the prohibition plus its reason. Reasons hold gates; bare imperatives cause false triggers.
prompt_patterns.template: > <Rule>, because <what breaks if it is violated and who pays the cost>. > Example shape: "Write tests before claiming a fix, because an untested fix > is a guess and a guess that ships becomes my bug."
prompt_patterns.raw:
- **Use when:** writing any standing instruction or guardrail.
- **Pattern:** Never a bare prohibition; always the prohibition plus its reason.
  Reasons hold gates; bare imperatives cause false triggers.
- **Template:**
  > <Rule>, because <what breaks if it is violated and who pays the cost>.
  > Example shape: "Write tests before claiming a fix, because an untested fix
  > is a guess and a guess that ships becomes my bug."

techniques.title: Live Preview as Verification Oracle (reflection loop)
techniques.what_it_does: After building, the agent runs the app in a live preview and then exercises it like a user — clicks buttons, fills forms, logs in to check user flows, spots bugs, fixes them, and re-runs. Community guides call this the signature step: the builder watches the agent test itself in a reflection loop.
techniques.why_it_works: A build is not verified by "code compiles"; it is verified by "the user flow works end to end." Making the agent its own first user catches integration bugs that static checks miss — the exact layer where vibe-coded apps silently break.
techniques.genesis_implementation: Give the hands module a `self_verify()` stage for app builds: after `run`, drive the app through its declared happy paths (via headless browser or API calls) and compare observed behavior against the acceptance criteria from the plan. A build cannot reach "publish" without a passing self-verification record. This is the idea→prototype analog of the Astra T-01 closed loop.
